title: WORTH Benchmark: Evidence Discovery under Not-Fully-Cooperative Information -- A Two-Episode Pilot
abstract: arXiv:2610.27597v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Existing reasoning evaluations typically provide task-relevant information to models as available premises, rarely examining concurrently how models discover evidence autonomously and how information presentation within narratives guides or obscures judgment. This paper proposes the WORTH Benchmark: models read original mystery narratives without clue annotations, autonomously select key clue sentences, identify case participants, and explain their reasoning process. The narrative materials are designed by professional authors such that evidence facilitating reasoning coexists with narrative arrangements that delay the revelation of truth. We report a pilot experiment under full-story conditions across two episodes, conducting a total of 70 formal runs on models, of which 67 runs are content-scorable. translated_title: WORTH基准：非完全合作信息下的证据发现——两集试点研究
translated_abstract: 现有的推理评估通常将任务相关信息作为可用前提提供给模型，很少同时考察模型如何自主发现证据，以及叙事中的信息呈现方式如何引导或遮蔽判断。本文提出WORTH基准：模型阅读没有线索标注的原创推理小说，自主选择关键线索句子、识别案件参与者，并解释其推理过程。叙事材料由专业作者设计，使促进推理的证据与延迟真相揭示的叙事安排并存。我们报告了在全篇故事条件下、跨越两集的试点实验，对模型共进行了70次正式运行，其中67次运行可进行内容评分。评分分别记录对作者指定关键线索句的命中情况和参与者选择情况；自然语言解释被用（原文在此处截断）……
tldr: 该论文提出WORTH基准，让模型在无线索标注的原创推理小说中自主发现关键证据、识别案件参与者并解释推理过程，以此评估模型在叙事信息不完全合作（证据与误导性安排并存）环境下的证据发现与判断能力。
en_tdlr: The paper proposes the WORTH Benchmark, where models read unannotated original mystery narratives to autonomously select key clue sentences, identify case participants, and explain their reasoning, evaluating evidence discovery under not-fully-cooperative information where helpful evidence coexists with narrative arrangements that delay truth revelation.
